artifacts.title: Wire graph-based execution into Validate mode
artifacts.body:
## Goal

Run the repository full test suite through litefactory before read-only validation of acceptance criteria, code, architecture and approved-plan compliance. Keep factory test execution distinct from reviewer authority, and preserve the separation of engineering completion and acceptance.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Versioned policy permitting factory-run full-suite checks before a read-only reviewer, preserving legacy rules for legacy instances.
2. Repository-declared full-suite execution and snapshot-bound retained results, including failed/missing prerequisites.
3. Read-only criterion/code/architecture/plan assessment using retained evidence.
4. Existing acceptance, reporting and external-effect projection with recovery; no implicit mode switch to fix code.
5. Integrated Implement→owner-selected Validate adoption and recovery verification.

Implementation work can overlap graph-based Implement once the test-execution contract is agreed. This parent does not grant the reviewer fresh-check or edit authority.

## Dependencies

Foundations for graph-based execution; Wire graph-based execution into Implement mode. Dependencies express rollout order, not automatic runtime mode selection.

## Agreed rollout boundaries

- One editable DOT workflow per mode; registered action names use `lf_<mode>_*`. Start with the standard shipped workflows.
- Pin active execution to immutable workflow/role definitions; bounded loops, durable owner replies, recovery and honest reporting are required.
- Preserve existing permission and result contracts. Users continue to select modes; completing a graph does not select the next mode.
- Keep both execution paths supported until the dedicated retirement. Build replacement team setup before retiring the old setup.
- Coordinate Implement's reduced test scope with Validate's full-suite entry so no testing gap is introduced.

## Origin and scope

Split from https://github.com/marioatcloudvane/litefactory/issues/230 after the owner approved the nine-main-issue roadmap. This issue starts in Research, with 3–6 candidate subissues to refine later. Temporal adoption, a visual editor, a marketplace and a commercial fleet-management service are outside this rollout.

artifacts.title: Retire legacy orchestration and execution
artifacts.body:
## Goal

Retire the old execution engine only after graph execution works across all five modes and required cutover evidence exists. Until this scope completes, support both execution engines, with each active instance pinned to its original engine and definition.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Inventory active/pending legacy work and define drain or explicitly authorized migration; preserve retained evidence/readers required by historical work.
2. Establish real cutover evidence across all five modes/providers plus recovery, permission and result-contract behavior; documented rollback/admission gates.
3. Switch eligible new work to graph defaults while pinned active work finishes safely.
4. Remove obsolete execution/orchestrator paths only after retirement criteria; update diagnostics, documentation and compatibility coverage.

Both execution paths remain supported until this parent meets its gate. Do not confuse this with the existing managed-feature workflow/content/submission versions or #274/#296 reader retirement. Adoption and retirement are distinct claims; offline tests do not replace required authentic host evidence.

## Dependencies

artifacts.title: Retire obsolete team setup
artifacts.body:
## Goal

Remove obsolete team installation and orchestration assets only after the graph-aware replacement is usable and remaining consumers have migrated. Do not remove reusable roles, skills, permissions or provenance merely because the old orchestrator is gone.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Inventory old installation/management surfaces and migrate remaining configurations and user overrides to the new graph-aware setup.
2. Verify fresh install, upgrade, pinned-instance recovery and rollback with no dependency on the obsolete setup.
3. Remove only superseded commands/rendered orchestration assets/compatibility plumbing, preserving needed role resources, provenance and permissions; finalize documentation.

Do not delete old setup and then build its replacement. Precise removal targets require Plan inventory.

## Dependencies

New team and workflow setup for graph-based execution; Retire legacy orchestration and execution. Dependencies express rollout order, not automatic runtime mode selection.

## Agreed rollout boundaries

- One editable DOT workflow per mode; registered action names use `lf_<mode>_*`. Start with the standard shipped workflows.
- Pin active execution to immutable workflow/role definitions; bounded loops, durable owner replies, recovery and honest reporting are required.
- Preserve existing permission and result contracts. Users continue to select modes; completing a graph does not select the next mode.
- Keep both execution paths supported until the dedicated retirement. Build replacement team setup before retiring the old setup.
- Coordinate Implement's reduced test scope with Validate's full-suite entry so no testing gap is introduced.
